title.title: Serre's intersection multiplicities are always positive
title.subtitle: Claim: $\chi(M,N) > 0$ over every regular local ring, including ramified mixed characteristic

plain: When two shapes meet in a point, an algebraic count of how they meet is always positive

beats.text: Serre's multiplicity: an alternating sum of Tor lengths, for supports that meet properly
Serre proved positivity with a field or unramified; Gabber got $\ge 0$ everywhere
The claim closes the last case: ramified mixed characteristic

steps: Move to huge 'perfectoid' rings where error terms vanish
There, the count matches its average over Galois twists
Each twist is positive, so the multiplicity is positive

achievement.label: Serre's positivity conjecture (1965)
achievement.context: Before: equal characteristic and unramified (Serre), nonnegativity (Gabber, 1995); ramified case open
achievement.note: The paper itself notes an earlier AI-assisted claim, posted in December 2025

voice.text: Serre's intersection multiplicity, an alternating sum of Tor lengths, should be positive.
Pass to perfectoid rings, average over Galois twists, and each twist is positive.
Claimed: positive, even in ramified mixed characteristic.

sources.quote: Serre (Algèbre locale, Multiplicités, 1965) proved it for equicharacteristic and unramified regular rings
Nonnegativity: Gabber (1995, via de Jong alterations
